verses.text: About this time King Herod began to arrest some who belonged to the church, to hurt them.
He had James, the brother of John, killed with a sword.
When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he arrested Peter too. This happened during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
After arresting Peter, Herod put him in prison, with four groups of four soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
So Peter was kept in prison, but the church kept praying hard to God for him.
The night before Herod was going to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, tied with two chains. Guards stood at the door watching the prison.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up. "Quick, get up!" he said. And the chains fell off Peter's wrists.
Then the angel said to him, "Get dressed and put on your sandals." Peter did so. "Put your coat on and follow me," the angel told him.
Peter followed him out of the prison, but he did not know that what the angel was doing was really happening. He thought he was seeing a vision.

They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading into the city. It opened for them by itself, and they went through it. They walked the length of one street, and suddenly the angel left him.
Then Peter came to himself and said, "Now I know for certain that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod's power, and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen."
When he understood this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John, who was also called Mark. Many people had gathered there and were praying.
Peter knocked at the outer door, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
When she knew Peter's voice, she was so happy that she ran back without opening the door. She told them, "Peter is at the door!"
They said to her, "You are out of your mind." But she kept saying it was true. So they said, "It must be his angel."
But Peter kept on knocking. When they opened the door and saw him, they were amazed.
Peter waved his hand to tell them to be quiet. He told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. "Tell James and the other brothers about this," he said. Then he left for another place.
In the morning there was a great fuss among the soldiers about what had happened to Peter.
Herod searched for him but could not find him. So he questioned the guards and ordered them to be put to death. Then Herod went from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

Herod had been very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him together, after winning over Blastus, a trusted servant of the king. They asked for peace, because their country got its food from the king's country.
On the chosen day Herod put on his royal robes, sat on his throne, and gave a speech to the people.
The people shouted, "This is the voice of a god, not of a man!"
At once an angel of the Lord struck Herod down, because he did not give glory to God. He was eaten by worms and died.
But God's word kept spreading, and more and more people believed.
When Barnabas and Saul had finished their work, they went back from Jerusalem, taking with them John, who was also called Mark.
